# Deep PR Checklist: Appointment Check-In

**Purpose**: Review whether check-in requirements are complete, unambiguous, internally consistent, and safely traceable before implementation.
**Created**: 2026-08-24
**Feature**: [Appointment Check-In specification](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are appointment check-in eligibility requirements complete for status, scope, start boundary, end boundary, and linked queue-entry creation? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK002 Are walk-in eligibility requirements complete for patient, doctor, branch membership, reception scope, and available scheduled-slot dependency? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003]
- [ ] CHK003 Are required queue-entry fields, their immutability, and source-specific appointment linkage specified without relying on unstated implementation behavior? [Completeness, Spec §FR-004–FR-006]
- [ ] CHK004 Are retrieval requirements complete for both UUID and queue-reference lookups, hospital/branch scope, and response content? [Completeness, Spec §FR-007; Contract §Retrieve entry]
- [ ] CHK005 Are audit requirements explicit about all required event fields, retention expectations, and prohibited PII categories? [Completeness, Spec §FR-010; Data Model §Audit events and invariants]
- [ ] CHK006 Are queue status lifecycle boundaries defined clearly enough to establish whether only `WAITING` is allowed in this feature? [Completeness, Spec §Assumptions; Data Model §Enums]

## Authorization, Privacy, and Audit

- [ ] CHK007 Are trusted staff identity, reception permission, hospital scope, and branch scope defined as server-side inputs for every protected operation? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001, FR-003, FR-007, FR-011]
- [ ] CHK008 Is the production fail-closed rule unambiguous about the required behavior before real authentication/staff identity is integrated? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK009 Are requirements explicit that ordinary request bodies, path/query values, and headers cannot establish actor, role, hospital, branch, or authorized scope? [Completeness, Spec §FR-011; Contract introductory paragraph]
- [ ] CHK010 Are non-disclosure rules consistent for unknown and out-of-scope appointment, patient, doctor, branch, and queue-entry resources? [Consistency, Spec §FR-008; Contract §§Check in appointment, Register walk-in, Retrieve entry]
- [ ] CHK011 Is the required distinction between unauthenticated, unauthorized, and non-disclosing out-of-scope failures specified consistently across all operations? [Clarity, Contract §§Check in appointment, Register walk-in]
- [ ] CHK012 Are audit requirements clear that the identity is trusted and that queue/appointment references do not expose patient contact, demographic, or clinical data? [Privacy, Spec §FR-010; Data Model §Audit events and invariants]

## Time, Queue, and Concurrency Rules

- [ ] CHK013 Is the check-in window specified unambiguously for exact start and end instants, including whether the scheduled end boundary is inclusive? [Clarity, Spec §FR-001; Research §Time and eligibility]
- [ ] CHK014 Are branch timezone requirements complete for appointment-date calculation, visit-date derivation, and queue ordering, including daylight-saving transitions? [Coverage, Spec §FR-009; Data Model §QueueEntry]
- [ ] CHK015 Are requirements clear about which persisted timestamp represents arrival/check-in time and how that timestamp is assigned? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009; Data Model §QueueEntry]
- [ ] CHK016 Is the deterministic queue tie-breaker defined for identical arrival times and is the reference guaranteed immutable for that purpose? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004, FR-009]
- [ ] CHK017 Are active-entry uniqueness rules explicit about status, patient, doctor, branch, and local visit date for both appointment and walk-in sources? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005; Data Model §Relationships and constraints]
- [ ] CHK018 Are concurrent duplicate-check-in and duplicate-walk-in outcomes fully specified, including idempotent versus conflict behavior? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002, FR-005; Contract §§Check in appointment, Register walk-in]
- [ ] CHK019 Are requirements defined for a concurrent appointment check-in and walk-in targeting the same patient, doctor, branch, and visit date? [Coverage, Spec §FR-005; Gap]
- [ ] CHK020 Are requirements defined for the outcome when queue-reference allocation collides or the persistence transaction fails after upstream eligibility is established? [Recovery, Gap]

## Lifecycle and Failure Scenarios

- [ ] CHK021 Are requirements complete for an appointment whose status changes, is cancelled, or expires while a check-in request is in flight? [Exception Flow, Spec §FR-001; Gap]
- [ ] CHK022 Are requirements clear about whether successful check-in must update appointment state and how queue creation and that update remain atomic? [Ambiguity, User Story 1; Plan §Integration Boundaries]
- [ ] CHK023 Are requirements defined for a scheduling availability decision that changes between walk-in eligibility evaluation and queue-entry persistence? [Recovery, Gap]
- [ ] CHK024 Are requirements explicit about whether a failed audit write prevents a check-in/walk-in from succeeding, or how recovery is handled? [Recovery, Spec §FR-010; Gap]
- [ ] CHK025 Are duplicate retry semantics specified for client timeouts where the first appointment check-in may have succeeded but no response was received? [Idempotency, Spec §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK026 Are out-of-scope and invalid-path error requirements defined without allowing error detail, timing, or response shape to reveal protected resource existence? [Privacy, Spec §FR-008; Contract introductory paragraph]

## Acceptance Criteria and Dependencies

- [ ] CHK027 Are SC-001 and SC-003 measurable with a stated workload, measurement boundary, and environment representative of PR/review validation? [Measurability, Spec §Success Criteria]
- [ ] CHK028 Is SC-002 precise about the concurrency level, request mix, assertion boundary, and definition of an active queue entry? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002]
- [ ] CHK029 Is SC-004 precise about the observable information that counts as disclosure across HTTP status, body, logs, and audit records? [Measurability, Spec §SC-004]
- [ ] CHK030 Are upstream patient, appointment, scheduling, branch-timezone, and audit contracts specified with availability, error, consistency, and ownership assumptions? [Dependencies, Spec §Assumptions; Plan §Integration Boundaries]
- [ ] CHK031 Are exclusions for booking, triage, consultation, no-show, billing, and queue calling clearly reconciled with all terms such as “appointment recorded as checked in” and “status”? [Consistency, Spec §Assumptions; User Story 1]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `$speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `$speckit-specify` and `$speckit-clarify`.
- Add comments or findings inline and link supporting artifacts where useful.
